image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of an African crocodile (Nile crocodile) resting on a sandy bank. The image focuses primarily on the head and upper torso. The mouth is slightly open, revealing interlocking teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal side and smoother scales near the jawline. One eye is clearly visible with a vertical slit pupil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point (V-shape), distinguishing it from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The jaws appear massive relative to the head size. Teeth are clearly visible, conical in shape, and appear to interlock correctly (specifically the large fourth lower tooth fitting into the upper jaw notch).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on the top ridge of the skull (dorsal). The pupil is a clear vertical slit. The surrounding anatomy suggests the presence of the nictitating membrane structure, though the membrane itself is retracted/transparent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The extreme tip of the snout is cut off by the right edge of the image frame; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body behind the head shows significant length and heavy armor plating consistent with a crocodilian.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal skin exhibits distinct, raised, rectangular bony plates (scutes) arranged in organized rows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy brown and grey-green. The texture is visibly rough and granular, matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The crocodile is lying on its belly; the ventral surface is completely occluded by the ground and the animal's own body mass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs or feet are visible in this tight head-and-shoulders crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely outside the frame.
